gap: No result ChatGPT got converts the head units' amp and preout ratings into decibels. Going from the Pioneer DMH-WT6000NEX's 14 W RMS x 4 (CTA-2006) to the Sony XAV-AX6000's 20 W RMS x 4 (CTA-2006) works out to only +1.5 dB (10·log10(20/14)). Their 5 V vs 4 V preouts differ by +1.9 dB (20·log10(5/4)). The XAV-9000ES's flagship price buys 0 dB over the AX6000 on either figure.
standout_why: I could not compare against the two cited Crutchfield pages (crutchfield.com/learn/best-car-stereo.html and crutchfield.ca/learn/best-touchscreen-car-stereos.html) because both, plus a session-URL copy, returned HTTP 403. CarAudioNow (cited) already gives the raw inputs per product: '20W RMS x 4 CTA-2006', '14W RMS x 4 CTA-2006', '5V' and '4V' preouts. TruePicked gives the same kind of RMS and preout figures, but for other models (XAV-AX5500, DMH-WT7600NEX, DMX9707S). World Wide Stereo's guide lists only '5-volt preamp outputs' for one Kenwood. None of the pages I could open convert these into dB gaps or compare them across picks. The new part is only the arithmetic; the inputs are already on a cited rival page.
decides: It supports ChatGPT's choice of the Sony XAV-AX6000 over the pricier picks rather than changing it. Built-in power and preamp voltage barely separate the AX6000, XAV-9000ES and DMX958XR (0 to +0.4 dB), so the extra ~$450 for the 9000ES or DMX958XR pays for tuning and features, not output. The DMH-WT6000NEX gives up 1.5 dB of built-in power and 1.9 dB of preout level for its 10.1-inch screen.
